reports.rendered_content: The normal graybox algorithm has a real implementation (8/10 architecture, 7.5/10 correctness) but is not production-ready (4/10 complex sets readiness). The implementation correctly uses deterministic surface sampling, joint-pair evaluation, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine. However, two blockers remain: imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because the extractor stores entire object AABBs as obstacles (rejecting interior points), and the geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports.

reports.rendered_content: The GLSL shader code implements a secondary panoramic projection sample. When projectedUseSecondary is active, it calculates the direction from the projected secondary origin to the world position, applies inverse pano yaw rotation, converts to equirectangular UV coordinates (with x wrapped via fract and y clamped to [0,1]), and samples the projectedSecondaryPanoMap texture multiplied by projectedExposure. The secondary sample is blended with the primary using a power-4 winner-takes-most weighting based on quality, visibility, and mode-specific dominance factors.
